auction_title: NBA Auctions Weekly: City and Classic Edition | Part II
title: Jimmy Butler Golden State Warriors 2025-2026 Game Worn City Edition Jersey
description_block: This home ‘City Edition’ jersey was worn in the 2nd Half by Jimmy Butler on November 24, 2025, when the Golden State Warriors played the Utah Jazz.  Butler finished with 18 points, 6 rebounds, 7 assists, and 1 steal. The Warriors beat the Jazz, 134-117.  Jimmy Butler is one of the most polarizing players in the NBA. His presence on the court has both endeared and frustrated fans and players alike. Butler's play style is characterized by his relentless intensity, versatility, and defensive prowess. He's a crafty driver who excels at attacking the basket and drawing fouls and possesses a smooth mid-range jumper. His improved three-point shooting makes him a scoring threat from all 3 levels on the floor. His offensive impact isn’t all about scoring- he's also an excellent facilitator, using his vision and basketball IQ to create opportunities for his teammates. Butler truly shines on the defensive end. He's a tenacious defender who takes pride in shutting down his opponents with his combination of size, strength, and quick hands. His defensive versatility allows him to guard multiple positions, making him a valuable asset for any team's defensive scheme. As the last player picked in the 1st round of the 2012 NBA Draft, nobody expected Butler to emerge into the superstar he has become. He’s earned 6 trips to the All-Star Game, been named to 5 All-NBA teams, and 5 NBA All-Defensive teams, and won the 2015 Most Improved Player award. After spending time with the Chicago Bulls, Minnesota Timberwolves, and Philadelphia 76ers, he has taken his career to the next level with the Miami Heat. This includes appearances in 2 NBA Finals, including one run as an 8 seed, and another Eastern Conference Finals appearance. His ability to flip a switch in the playoffs, highlighted by his career-high 56-point effort against the Milwaukee Bucks, has earned him the nickname ‘Playoff Jimmy.’ At the time of cataloging, Butler has career averages of 18.4 points per game, 5.4 rebounds per game, and 4.4 assists per game. This jersey has been photomatched by Sotheby’s Photomatching.

description_block: This home ‘Classic Edition’ jersey was worn by Julius Randle on November 29, 2025 when the Minnesota Timberwolves played the Boston Celtics. Julius Randle’s promise as an NBA player was clear from his single season at the University of Kentucky. In the 2013-2014 campaign, Randle averaged a double-double, with 15 points and 10.4 rebounds per game while helping Kentucky reach the National Championship Game. Randle was drafted 7th in the 1st round of the 2014 NBA Draft. Despite a devastating injury in his debut, the Lakers remained patient. Randle would recover and averaged a double-double in his second season. After two more strong seasons in L.A., Randle signed with the Pelicans, where he notched his first scoring average of over 20 points. After a season in New Orleans, Randle signed with the New York Knicks, and in the Big Apple Randle blossomed. Randle led the Knicks to their first playoff appearance in eight seasons in 2020-2021, was named an All-Star as well as Most Improved Player, and was named to the All-NBA Second Team. After teaming up with Jalen Brunson, Randle was again named an All-Star in 2023 and earned a place on the All-NBA 3rd Team. He and Brunson led the Knicks to their first playoff win in a decade when the Knicks beat the Cleveland Cavaliers. Before the 2024-25 season, Randle was traded to the Timberwolves as part of a blockbuster deal that sent Karl-Anthony Towns to the Knicks. The Timberwolves hope their new trio of Randle, Anthony Edwards, and Rudy Gobert can lead them to their first NBA Finals in franchise history. At the time of cataloging, Randle has career averages of 19.3 points, 9 rebounds, and 3.9 assists per game. Randle is a 3-time NBA All-Star and earned the 2021 Most Improved Player Award. description_block: This home ‘City Edition’ jersey was worn by Paul George on December 2, 2025, when the Philadelphia 76ers played the Washington Wizards. George finished with 11 points, 5 rebounds, and 1 steal. The 76ers beat the Wizards, 121-102. Paul George's journey to stardom began in 2010 when he was drafted by the Indiana Pacers with the 10th overall pick. George quickly made a name for himself with his exceptional athleticism and two-way play, earning his first NBA All-Star selection in 2013 and the Most Improved Player award that same year. After successful stints with the Indiana Pacers and Oklahoma City Thunder, George joined the Los Angeles Clippers before signing a four-year, $212 million contract with the Philadelphia 76ers in July 2024. In Philadelphia, George has formed a highly anticipated trio alongside Joel Embiid and Tyrese Maxey. At the time of cataloging, he has career averages of 20.5 points per game, 6.2 rebounds per game, and 3.7 assists per game. He is a nine-time NBA All-Star, a six-time All-NBA selection, a four-time All-Defensive Team selection, and the 2012–13 NBA Most Improved Player. This jersey has been photomatched by PSA.
